dhp334:1: For a human who lives life heedlessly
dhp334:2: craving increases like a clinging creeper,
dhp334:3: he rushes from one place to another
dhp334:4: like a monkey desiring fruit in the forest.
dhp335:1: That one who is overcome by these low cravings and attachments in the world,
dhp335:3: for him griefs increase like grass that has had heavy rain.
dhp336:1: Whoever overcomes this low craving in the world, which is difficult to get past,
dhp336:3: griefs fall from him like a drop of water from a lotus.
dhp337:2: “Good luck to as many as have assembled here”,
dhp337:3: dig up the root of craving,
dhp337:4: like one seeking the root (digs up) grass,
dhp337:5: do not let Māra push you down again like a stream (pushes down) the reed.
dhp338:1: Just as when the root remains firm and untroubled
dhp338:2: though the tree was cut down, it grows again,
dhp338:3: so when the tendency to craving is not rooted out
dhp338:4: this suffering appears again and again.
dhp339:1: He in whom the thirty-six streams flow pleasantly and strong,
dhp339:3: the one with wrong view, is carried away by his passionate intentions.
dhp340:1: Streams are flowing everywhere, the creepers remain where they grow,
dhp340:3: seeing this, cut the creeper’s root that has arisen with wisdom.
dhp341:1: * There are flowing streams of affection and
dhp341:4: those people undergo both birth and old age.
dhp342:2: crawl round like a hare in a trap,
dhp342:4: they come back again and again to suffering for a long time.
dhp343:2: crawl round like a hare in a trap,
dhp343:4: the monk who longs for dispassion for himself.
dhp344:1: The one who is free from desires, who is intent on the forest,
dhp344:2: (though) free from the forest, runs back to the forest,
dhp344:3: come here and look at that person,
dhp344:4: (though) free, he runs back to bondage.
dhp345:1: That bondage is not so strong say the wise,
dhp345:2: that is made of iron or wood or reeds,
dhp345:3: * impassioned and excited they seek out
dhp345:4: jewels and earrings and children and wives –
dhp346:1: that bondage is strong say the wise,
dhp346:2: dragging down the lax, hard to get free from,
dhp346:3: having cut this down they wander about
dhp346:4: seeking nothing, abandoning the happiness in pleasure.
dhp347:1: Those who are impassioned by passion follow the stream
dhp347:2: like a spider a web made by itself,
dhp347:3: having cut this away the wise proceed,
dhp348:1: Be free of the past, be free of the future,
dhp348:2: be free of the present, after crossing over (all) existence,
dhp348:3: with mind liberated in every way,
dhp348:4: you will not return to birth and old age.
dhp349:1: For a person crushed by thoughts
dhp349:2: and pierced by passion, contemplating the attractive,
dhp349:4: this surely makes the bond more firm.
dhp350:1: Whoever has delight in the calming of thoughts,
dhp350:2: who always mindfully cultivates what is unattractive,
dhp350:4: he will cut off the bond of Māra.
dhp351:1: Having gone to the end, without trembling,
dhp351:3: cutting off the darts of existence,
dhp351:4: this one is his final body.
dhp352:2: skilled in words and their explanation,
dhp352:3: knowing how syllables are arranged, which come before and which after,
dhp352:5: the one in his final body is said to be (a great person), one of great wisdom.
dhp353:3: having given up everything, liberated through craving’s destruction,
dhp353:4: when having deep knowledge myself, who should I point to (as Teacher)?
dhp354:1: The gift of the Dhamma surpasses all other gifts,
dhp354:2: the taste of the Dhamma surpasses all other tastes,
dhp354:3: the love of the Dhamma surpasses all other loves,
dhp354:4: destruction of craving overcomes all suffering.
dhp355:1: Riches destroy the stupid one who does not seek the way beyond,
dhp355:3: through his craving for riches the stupid one destroys others and himself.
dhp356:1: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds,
dhp356:2: these people are ruined by passion,
dhp356:3: therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without passion.
dhp357:1: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds, these people are ruined by hatred,
dhp357:3: therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without hatred.
dhp358:1: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds, these people are ruined by delusion,
dhp358:3: therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without delusion.
dhp359:1: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds, these people are ruined by desire,
dhp359:3: therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without desire.
